title: Act IV, Scene III

teacherSummary.text: Juliet sends her mother and the Nurse away and, alone, imagines all that could go wrong: the potion might be poison, she might wake before Romeo, she might go mad among the bones. She drinks to Romeo.

I have a faint cold fear thrills through my veins,

Nurse!

Ay, those attires are best: but, gentle nurse,
I pray thee, leave me to myself to-night;
For I have need of many orisons
To move the heavens to smile upon my state,
Which, well thou know’st, is cross and full of sin.

segments.script: First, meaning. I read “What if it be a poison, which the friar / Subtly hath minister’d to have me dead” slowly and put it in my own words: Alone, Juliet wonders whether the Friar has given her poison to kill her and hide his part in her marriage. Next, craft. I notice the string of anxious questions, as she imagines every way the plan could go wrong. The strongest word is “poison”: it is her worst fear, that her trusted helper might betray her. Then, effect. What does Juliet fear before taking the potion? My answer: Juliet's doubts and terrors show her real courage, because she drinks the potion anyway; she chooses faith in Romeo over safety.
